archetypes.name: Predictive Coding
archetypes.description: Prediction error minimization via hierarchical inference and precision-weighted belief updating. Brain generates top-down predictions; mismatches trigger learning.
theoretical_basis: Friston, K. (2010). The free-energy principle. Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 11(2), 127-138.
Clark, A. (2013). Whatever next? Predictive brains, situated agents, and the future of cognitive science. Behavioral and Brain Sciences, 36(3), 181-204.
Rao, R. P., & Ballard, D. H. (1999). Predictive coding in the visual cortex. Nature Neuroscience, 2(5), 490-492.

precision_weight.name: precision_weight
precision_weight.description: Relative weighting of prediction errors by inverse variance. Higher = more weight to high-precision (low-variance) errors.

learning_rate.name: learning_rate
learning_rate.description: Rate at which predictions adjust based on errors.

hierarchical_depth.name: hierarchical_depth
hierarchical_depth.description: Number of hierarchical levels in predictive model.

domain_examples.description: Visual complexity preference mediated by prediction error magnitude. Optimal complexity balances novelty (positive prediction error) with comprehension.
Grouping of sound components into coherent auditory objects via prediction error minimization. Unexpected acoustic changes trigger reanalysis.
Expected vs. actual thermal sensation generates corrective responses. Habituation reflects updating of thermal predictions.
Prediction errors about others' behavior drive social learning and theory-of-mind updates.
Prediction errors about spatial layout trigger corrective navigation and environmental learning.

archetypes.computational_signature: error = observation - prediction; prediction_update = learning_rate * precision_weight * error; belief_t+1 = belief_t + learning_rate * error

archetypes.name: Homeostatic Regulation
archetypes.description: Deviation from setpoint triggers corrective responses via negative feedback. System returns to equilibrium with adaptation over time.
theoretical_basis: Cannon, W. B. (1932). The wisdom of the body. Norton.
Barrett, L. F., & Simmons, W. K. (2015). Interoceptive predictions in the brain. Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 16(7), 419-429.
Stephan, K. E., & Mathys, C. (2014). Computational approaches to major psychiatric disorders. Current Opinion in Behavioral Sciences, 4, 85-92.

setpoint.name: setpoint
setpoint.description: Target value for regulated variable (e.g., temperature in Celsius).

gain.name: gain
gain.description: Sensitivity of corrective response to deviation from setpoint.

adaptation_time_constant.name: adaptation_time_constant
adaptation_time_constant.description: Timescale over which setpoint adapts to sustained deviations.

domain_examples.description: Preferred temperature range adapts based on outdoor climate and prior experience. Setpoint shifts seasonally.
Chronotype setpoint shifts with environmental light exposure. Entrainment to local dawn/dusk.
Preferred arousal level varies by task and context. Deviation triggers compensatory behaviors.
Caloric intake homeostasis with long-term weight set-point. Adaptation to chronic caloric restriction/surplus.

archetypes.computational_signature: drive = |current_state - setpoint|; response = gain * drive; setpoint_t+1 = setpoint_t + adaptation_rate * (mean_recent_state - setpoint_t)

archetypes.name: Accumulation to Bound
archetypes.description: Evidence accumulates over time until reaching a decision threshold. Generates characteristic reaction time distributions with speed-accuracy tradeoff.
theoretical_basis: Ratcliff, R., & McKoon, G. (2008). The diffusion decision model. Psychological Review, 115(2), 236-285.
Frazier, P., & Yu, A. J. (2008). Optimal knapsack problems with stochastic rewards. Journal of Problem Solving, 2(1), 7.
Shiffrin, R. M., Lee, M. D., Kim, W., & Wagenmakers, E. J. (2008). A survey of model evaluation approaches with a tutorial on hierarchical Bayesian methods. Cognitive Science, 32(8), 1248-1284.

threshold.name: threshold
threshold.description: Boundary at which decision is triggered.

drift_rate.name: drift_rate
drift_rate.description: Mean rate of evidence accumulation. Positive = bias toward one decision.

noise_sigma.name: noise_sigma
noise_sigma.description: Standard deviation of noise in evidence accumulation process.

domain_examples.description: Initial visual encounter generates weak evidence; dwell time allows accumulation to preference boundary.
At intersection, accumulating environmental cues (signage, visual continuity) lead to route choice decision.
Accumulation of comfort cues (thermal, social, configurational) determines engagement or withdrawal.
Evidence of threats accumulates; once threshold crossed, defensive or avoidance behavior triggered.

archetypes.computational_signature: evidence(t) = evidence(t-1) + drift_rate*dt + noise*sqrt(dt); decision made when |evidence| >= threshold; RT proportional to (threshold / drift_rate)

archetypes.name: Competitive Selection
archetypes.description: Multiple options compete via mutual inhibition and lateral interactions until one 'wins'. Implements selective attention and choice.
theoretical_basis: Desimone, R., & Duncan, J. (1995). Neural mechanisms of selective attention. Annual Review of Neuroscience, 18(1), 193-222.
Usher, M., & McClelland, J. L. (2001). On the time course of perceptual choice. Psychological Review, 108(3), 550-592.
Gershman, S. J., Horvitz, E. J., & Tenenhaus, J. K. (2015). Computational rationality: A converging paradigm for intelligence in brains, minds, and machines. Science, 349(6245), 273-278.

inhibition_strength.name: inhibition_strength
inhibition_strength.description: Strength of lateral inhibition between competitors.

time_to_selection.name: time_to_selection
time_to_selection.description: Typical time from stimulus to winner determination.

domain_examples.description: Among multiple salient features, lateral inhibition determines which receives attentional resources.
Multiple potential saccade targets compete; winner becomes next fixation point.
At decision point, multiple route options compete; choice reflects relative salience and familiarity.
Among aesthetic options, competitive processes amplify subtle differences into clear preferences.
Multiple behavioral options compete; motor system implements winner via winner-take-all dynamics.

archetypes.computational_signature: activation_i(t) = input_i - inhibition_strength * sum(activation_j, j≠i); winner = argmax(activation); selection_strength = activation_winner - activation_second_best

archetypes.name: Gated Propagation
archetypes.description: Information flow is multiplicatively or additively modulated by a gate signal. Implements selective attention, working memory constraints, and stress responses.
theoretical_basis: Miller, E. K., & Cohen, J. D. (2001). An integrative theory of prefrontal cortex function. Annual Review of Neuroscience, 24(1), 167-202.
Hasher, L., & Zacks, R. T. (1988). Working memory, comprehension, and aging. The Psychology of Learning and Motivation, 22, 193-225.
Arousal-Modulation Theory: Easterbrook (1959) and modern variants.

gate_threshold.name: gate_threshold
gate_threshold.description: Minimum gate signal strength to allow propagation.

modulation_gain.name: modulation_gain
modulation_gain.description: Strength of gate effect on information flow.

gate_time_constant.name: gate_time_constant
gate_time_constant.description: Timescale over which gate transitions occur.

domain_examples.description: High arousal narrows attention; gate signal from sympathetic system restricts information access.
Prefrontal gating determines which information remains active in working memory.
HPA axis activation gates down non-essential processing; focuses on threat-relevant information.
Cognitive control gates emotional information via dorsolateral PFC inhibition.
High task demand gates out environmental awareness; inattentional blindness results.

archetypes.computational_signature: gate_signal_t = f(gate_control); output = gate_signal * input_with_gain + (1 - gate_signal) * baseline; propagation_rate depends on gate_signal

archetypes.name: Convergent State Monitoring
archetypes.description: Multiple noisy sensors or modalities integrate into a coherent state estimate. Confidence reflects agreement (low conflict) among sensors.
theoretical_basis: Stein, B. E., & Meredith, M. A. (1993). The merging of the senses. MIT Press.
Stein, B. E. (2012). The new handbook of multisensory processes. MIT Press.
Körding, K. P., & Wolpert, D. M. (2004). Bayesian integration in sensorimotor learning. Nature, 427(6971), 244-247.

conflict_threshold.name: conflict_threshold
conflict_threshold.description: Variance threshold above which conflict signal is generated.

integration_window.name: integration_window
integration_window.description: Temporal window over which signals are integrated.

domain_examples.description: Visual, auditory, and tactile signals converge into unified percept. Conflict detection generates discordance signals.
Safety, nature presence, and fascination converge into restoration judgment. High agreement = strong restorative quality.
Nociceptive, affective, and cognitive-evaluative channels integrate into pain experience. Central sensitization = weight shift.
Visual continuity, functional logic, and navigational clarity converge into coherence judgment.
Visual, vestibular, proprioceptive, and landmark information converge to localize self in space.

archetypes.computational_signature: state_estimate = sum(weight_i * sensor_i) / sum(weight_i); confidence = 1 - variance(weighted_residuals); conflict_i = (sensor_i - state_estimate)^2
